title: Shared federal facilities can convert specialized infrastructure into mission work and cost recovery while creating capacity dependence
source_unit: GAO review of National Nuclear Security Administration Strategic Partnership Projects using NNSA and contractor data, site visits, interviews, and selected agreement review
geography: Eight NNSA sites in the United States; detailed site visits at Kansas City, Livermore, Los Alamos, Nevada, and Sandia

denominator.unit: NNSA sites conducting Strategic Partnership Projects; enterprise-wide project and reimbursed-cost data

total_reimbursed_costs.unit: approximately US dollars in constant FY2024 dollars across more than 20,000 agreements

annual_reimbursed_activity.value: between $2 billion and $3 billion per year

national_security_share.unit: percent of agreements categorized by NNSA as national-security related

partner_mission_dependence.value: all nine interviewed federal partners said SPP was essential to completing their mission; some capabilities were described as available only at NNSA sites

mission_or_public_outcome.value: not established as a linked outcome across projects
mission_or_public_outcome.unit: missing project-level capability, service, public-benefit, or external-response endpoint

observations.method: GAO analysis of NNSA and contractor data, documentation, five site visits, interviews, and a nongeneralizable sample of 13 agreements; constant FY2024 dollars used for trend comparisons.
observations.uncertainty: The project sample is not generalizable to all agreements, partner-essentiality is interview evidence, and reimbursed work does not itself establish mission performance, public benefit, strategic autonomy, or external response.
observations.subgroup: NNSA sites, federal and nonfederal SPP partners, NNSA and contractor staff, and specialized facility users; public households and affected communities are not directly observed.
observations.counterinterpretation: Shared use can preserve specialized capabilities and reduce idle capacity without proving that every project advanced core missions; mission dependence may reflect lack of substitutes rather than efficient or equitable allocation.

observations.period: Fiscal year 2024 indirect-cost and capacity observation

denominator.unit: NNSA sites; indirect-cost table covers seven sites with available percentages

indirect_costs_reimbursed.unit: approximately US dollars received from SPP partners in FY2024

indirect_cost_share.unit: percent of $2.66 billion total SPP reimbursed costs in the table; seven sites ranged from 44% to 57%

facility_utilization.value: SPP increased use of existing specialized facilities and systems and contributed to maintenance and operations

capacity_constraint.value: some sites limited or reduced SPP growth because of competing mission work, infrastructure, or personnel pressure

public_cost_and_mission_outcome.unit: missing counterfactual public cost, facility condition, project quality, household effect, or later mission result

observations.method: GAO analysis of FY2024 site-level reimbursed and indirect-cost data plus interviews about shared facilities, staffing, maintenance, and the effects of rebalancing partnership work.
observations.uncertainty: Savannah River indirect costs were unavailable; cost recovery and utilization are not the same as net savings, facility condition, public value, or successful mission delivery.
observations.subgroup: NNSA programs, SPP partners, site personnel, and facility/capability budgets; no household-level ratepayer or resident incidence is reported.
observations.counterinterpretation: Partner-funded overhead may reduce costs borne by NNSA programs while also consuming scarce staff and facilities; a higher utilization rate can coexist with congestion or reduced flexibility for core work.

boundary: This record establishes realized shared use of specialized federal infrastructure, partner dependence, reimbursed work, indirect-cost recovery, and capacity constraints. It does not establish net savings, project quality, facility condition, public household benefit, equitable allocation, delivered mission capability, substitute availability, or changed geopolitical leverage.
